prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universally “best” dentist for implants in Phoenix — the right provider depends on your needs (single tooth vs full-arch), medical/dental history, insurance/budget, and whether you prefer a specialist or a general dentist who places implants. Here’s how to find the best provider for you and what to look for.

Who usually places implants
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons and periodontists: specialists with advanced surgical training — often best for complex cases (bone grafting, sinuses, extractions).
- Prosthodontists: specialists in restoring implants and making the crowns/bridges/prostheses look/function optimally.
- General dentists with advanced implant training: can be excellent for straightforward cases and offer a single-provider workflow.

How to choose — checklist of qualifications and capabilities
- Training: DMD/DDS plus additional residency or fellowship in oral surgery, periodontics, prosthodontics, or evidence of advanced implant training (continuing education, mentorships).
- Experience: number of implants placed per year, years placing implants, examples/portfolio (before & after photos).
- Technology: in-house CBCT (3D imaging), digital planning, guided implant surgery, CAD/CAM restorations.
- Teamwork: coordination with a prosthodontist if the surgeon doesn’t restore the crown; a single team that does both can simplify care.
- Sedation options: nitrous, oral sedation, IV sedation (if needed).
- Follow-up and warranty: clear aftercare plan and any guarantees on restorations.
- Reviews and referrals: recent patient reviews, referrals from your general dentist, and peer recommendations.
- Board certification/associations: AAOMS, AAP (periodontics), ABO (prosthodontics) — membership is a good sign but not required.

Questions to ask when you call/consult
- How many implants do you place each year? What percent succeed?
- Who will place the implant and who will make the final crown/bridge?
- Do you use CBCT and guided surgery? Do you offer same-day/teeth-in-a-day options?
- Will I need bone grafting or a sinus lift? If so, do you do those in-house?
- Can I see case photos or patient testimonials for cases like mine?
- What are the total costs (surgery + implant + abutment + crown) and financing options?
- What is your complication protocol and follow-up schedule?

Red flags
- Vague answers about training/experience
- No imaging or unwillingness to use CBCT for planning
- Extremely low price compared to local market with no explanation
- Poor/inconsistent patient reviews about outcomes or communication

Cost and timeline (rough)
- Single implant (placement + abutment + crown): commonly ranges roughly $3,000–$6,000 in the U.S. (varies widely)
- Healing/osseointegration: typically 3–6 months (can be shorter with immediate loading in select cases)
- Complex cases (grafts, sinus lifts, full-arch): higher cost and longer timeline
